captions.text: Recap of chapter 32: load_model switched models in one line.
A bigger local model dropped the eval from 113 to 14, with no error.
GeminiModel translated our messages by hand, with the key kept in .env.
And SpendLimit stopped at a dollar limit. Every call now has a price.
Today's black box: what a run costs, in money and in time.
Measure each run, then decide what to cut. Some cuts cost more than they save.
Meter is a hook. After each model call, it keeps the time and the token counts.
With prices, it adds up what the run cost. A local model costs nothing.
One question on 7B. Two calls: one to search, one to answer. The second reads twice as much.
The same on Flash-Lite. Predict: how long does a call take?
The first call took 34.8 seconds for 18 tokens. The next took 1.5. One run tells you little.
What does each call send? The system prompt and tool descriptions go every time, unchanged.
Search results are the biggest part. The question is 4%.
Across a whole pass, search results were 43% on 7B and 65% on Flash-Lite.
And the time? The model took 117 of 120 seconds. The tools took 3.
So send fewer search results. Predict: fewer tokens, but what happens to the score?
One result cut tokens by a fifth, and the score from 112 to 99. Every cut lost points here.
On a paid model: one result is cheapest per right answer. Only five got every question right.
The measurement can't choose for you. It tells you the price of each choice.
People feel the first words, not the last. On 7B they arrive in a few hundredths of a second.
On Flash-Lite they arrive with the whole reply. That's us: our GeminiModel doesn't stream.
And the same short question took 1.7 seconds once and 17.5 another. One timing proves nothing.
A cloud model waits on someone else's computers, so we can wait for several at once.
Each question gets a new agent, because hooks keep state. Results come back in order.
Predict: eight at once. Flash-Lite went from 447 seconds to 64, with the same score.
7B on one Mac barely changed. And running at once saves time, not money.
Caching: send the same long prompt again, and part may come from the cache, at a tenth of the price.
Flash-Lite cached 2,033 tokens a call, and charged 37% less.
3.6 Flash cached nothing, every time. You can't count on caching. Check it.
Measure first. The question was 4% of what we sent, so shortening it would save nothing.
Check every cut against the eval. A cut that loses points isn't a saving.
Count cost per right answer, not per call.
For time, look at the model first. Run at once on the cloud, and stream when people watch.
Five exercises: shares, cost per right answer, cached cost, a timer and running at once.
You've finished when you see 5 passed.
